title: Holding Entries Without the Headache
hook: Cleared to hold. Which entry? You've got until the fix to decide.

scenes.narration: Alright kid, thirty seconds. Holding entries. Three ways in, zero excuses.
Draw one line through the fix, seventy degrees off the inbound course. Three sectors, three entries.
The big slice? Fly direct. Cross the fix, turn outbound. Direct is free money, kid. Take it.
The narrow sliver? Teardrop. Thirty degrees into the protected side, then back inbound. The wide wedge? Parallel. Outbound on the course, then turn back in.
Big slice direct. Sliver teardrop. Wedge parallel. Nobody grades your geometry, kid — just stay in protected airspace.
Homework: A I M five dash three dash eight. It's a page-turner.

quiz.question: The three standard holding entries are:
quiz.explanation: AIM 5-3-8 recommends direct, parallel, and teardrop entries based on your heading relative to the holding course.

quiz.question: The recommended entry sectors are divided by a line drawn at what angle to the inbound holding course?
quiz.explanation: The 70° line through the fix splits the non-direct region into the parallel and teardrop sectors.

quiz.question: In a teardrop entry, after crossing the fix you fly...
choices: ~30° off the outbound course on the holding side, then turn to intercept inbound
Parallel to the inbound course on the non-holding side
quiz.explanation: Teardrop: proceed on an outbound track ~30° to the holding side, then turn back to intercept the inbound course. (AIM 5-3-8)
